tools.name: find_place
tools.description: Look up a US city or town by name (free, no key). Returns matches with their census place GEOID and centre point (lon/lat). The entry point: feed a GEOID to blocks_in_area, or a centre to walkability_summary.

tools.name: get_catalog
tools.description: List the travel modes and the destination-type taxonomy (free, no key). Use it to resolve type names to the numeric ids the other tools take. Modes are walk, bike, transit — there is no drive mode.

tools.name: walkability_summary
tools.description: Fastest travel time from a location to each destination category, by mode (metered: 1 token per returned row). One origin: block_geoid or lat+lon. Many origins (up to 250): block_geoids or points — one batch call and one rate-limit request, with rows tagged by origin. Batching saves requests and con

tools.name: nearby_pois
tools.description: Nearby points of interest and the travel time to each, from a location (metered: 1 token per returned row). One origin: block_geoid or lat+lon; keep limit small to control spend and context size. Many origins (up to 250): block_geoids or points — one batch call and one rate-limit request, rows tagge

tools.name: isochrone
tools.description: The area reachable from a location within a time budget, as GeoJSON contours (metered: 10 tokens per contour). Give block_geoid or lat+lon. Defaults to a single 30-minute contour; ask for more only when needed (bodies can be large).

tools.name: blocks_in_area
tools.description: Per-block travel times for every census block in an area (metered: 1 token per returned row). Give place_geoid (from find_place) for a whole city, or center {lat, lon} + radius_m. Rows carry a numeric mode_id.

tools.name: get_token_balance
tools.description: Check the token balance of the API key in use, without spending any tokens. Works even at a zero balance. Requires the Authorization bearer key.

tools.name: request_sign_in
tools.description: Start free sign-up for the user: email them a six-digit code. The user must read the code from their own inbox and give it to you, then call redeem_code. This is how an agent gets the user an API key (5,000 free tokens, no card).

tools.name: redeem_code
tools.description: Complete sign-up with the six-digit code the user received, and return a new API key (shown once). Call request_sign_in first. The key grants 5,000 free tokens; store it and pass it as the Authorization bearer on future calls.

tools.name: join_close_plus
tools.description: Get a Stripe Checkout URL for the Close+ membership ($10/month: 5,000 API tokens granted monthly plus member features on the close.city map). The user pays in their own browser: give them the returned URL and stop. Needs a fresh six-digit code from request_sign_in, read by the user from their own in

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "join_close_plus" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: request_sign_in, join_close_plus · Private data: walkability_summary, nearby_pois, isochrone, blocks_in_area, get_token_balance, request_sign_in, redeem_code, join_close_plus · Public sink: request_sign_in.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: request_sign_in, join_close_plus · Private data: walkability_summary, nearby_pois, isochrone, blocks_in_area, get_token_balance, request_sign_in, redeem_code, join_close_plus · Public sink: request_sign_in

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "walkability_summary" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Fastest travel time from a location to each destination category, by mode (metered: ~1 token per returned row). Give either block_geoid or lat+lon. A missing category means it is not reachable within 30 minutes." → after: "Fastest travel time from a location to each destination category, by mode (metered: 1 token per returned row). One origin: block_geoid or lat+lon. Many origins (up to 250): block_geoids or points — one batch call and one rate-limit request, with rows tagged by origin. Batching saves requests and con"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
